articleTitle: Computer generated solid arrow display of 3-D vector fields
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Fields in Three Dimensions
abstract: A new method of display of vector fields is described which uses an arrow of fixed proportions to display the magnitude and direction of a vector at each point at which it is known. The arrow head has thickness and the whole arrow is scaled in proportion to the magnitude of the field so that the orientation perpendicular to the plane of the paper is indicated by the body of the head and foreshortening of the image. It has applications in all branches of engineering and science where calculations give numerical values of field vectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated approach to the solution of 3D engineering problems in a workstation environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Fields in Three Dimensions
abstract: The authors detail the design and development of a fully interactive system capable of solving 2- and 3-dimensional problems arising in the design of electrical apparatus. This system is known as 'SLIM' (Stafford Laboratory Integrated Modelling) and will eventually be used in the design areas by design staff.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhanced display functions using a 3D graphics processor with integrated user interface system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Fields in Three Dimensions
abstract: The ideas that lead to the creation of a post processing and display system for electromagnetic fields are described. The system integrates the user interface with a mathematical function interpreter that contains a set of state variables which are maintained by the program. This allows scalar and vector functions of the solutions to be calculated and displayed quite generally. The software has been implemented on the latest Tektronix 3D graphics workstation and fully utilises this powerful graphics processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Fields in Three Dimensions
abstract: The post viewer concept introduced by E.M. Freeman is discussed for EM field displays and global quantities. The computation of the solution plane and the various post viewing modes are then examined as well as some of the more important functions available on the post viewer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Display of field quantities in a 3D electromagnetics program
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Visualisation of Fields in Three Dimensions
abstract: Summary form only given. A general program, known as MEGA, has been developed for solving 2D and 3D electromagnetic problems. The discussion mainly concerns the pre- and post-processor sections of MEGA. The 3D meshes are derived from 2D meshes by 'extruding' along one coordinate. Advantages of this approach include easy data handling in the program, also a user can visualise where he is in the model and move around very easily. A major disadvantage is that some devices, at worst, cannot be meshed in this way and, at best, can be modelled only by including much redundant detail in the problem. In the post processing state it is important that a user can easily view any of the quantities which are important to the design of a device. This is done by 'slicing' up the device in an arbitrary way and displaying the required quantities on the surface of the 'cuts'. Holography opens up the possibility of viewing computer created models almost in 3D. Some of these techniques are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
